In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of semantic memory and its neural basis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

category specific semantic memory deficits are due to a combination of disease related atrophy in the neural substrate for semantic memory and the reliance of the patient on this neural substrate for semantic processing.

the category-specific semantic memory deficit in Alzheimer's disease is due to a combination of disease in regions of the semantic memory network that are normally involved in the representation of natural kinds, and the inability to compensate for the deficit by using regions outside of that network that are typically not involved in the representation and access of semantic information for natural kinds.

the neural network that supports semantic memory for objects in Alzheimer's disease is dependent on both modality-specific association areas that support perceptual knowledge and heteromodal areas that support access to this knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
category-specific semantic memory deficits in Alzheimer's disease are related to disease in a network of brain areas, including modality-specific association and heteromodal areas.
category specific memory deficits in Alzheimer's disease are due in part to a loss of access to a large-scale neural semantic network.

the neural substrate of category-specific semantic memory in healthy adults is an extensive network of regions including modality-specific association cortices and heteromodal cortices important for accessing this information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

semantic memory for natural kinds may depend more than manufactured objects on the same neural system that supports visual perception, and that Alzheimer's patients may have a deficit for natural kinds because of disease in the neural system that underlies semantic memory.

semantic memory is not only dependent on the modality-specific cortex where features are stored, but is also dependent on heteromodal areas that are important for accessing these feature knowledge representations.
category-specific semantic deficits may result from a breakdown in the large-scale network that supports semantic knowledge.
